card.title: Ampere's circuital law and its applications

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Ampere's law is applied by a path that matches the symmetry. Inside a uniform wire only the inner share of the current counts and B grows with r. A toroid's field is μ0 N I over the circular circumference, and an ideal toroid has no field on a path that encloses nothing.

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Governing equation for "Ampere's circuital law and its applications" — state with units, then use in one numerical.
Wire: B × 2πr = μ0 I
Toroid: B = μ0 N I /(2π r)

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: ❌ state the rule without its limit → ✅ note when it applies / stops applying.  ·  ❌ no diagram → ✅ add one labelled figure / structured list.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: At the surface both wire formulas give μ0 I /(2π R).  ·  A tightly wound toroid has little field outside.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: The applications are the reason the law is taught. You invent an Amperian path that follows the suspected field, write B times the length if B is constant, and set that equal to μ0 I_enclosed.  ·  Outside a long straight wire the path is a circle and the whole current is enclosed. Inside a uniform cylindrical wire, at radius r smaller than the wire, only the current in the inner cross-section is enclosed, so I_enc = I (r^2/R^2).

rows.text: Same law, applied.  ·  The path is chosen, not measured.  ·  A thick wire needs the current inside radius r only.  ·  The toroid is the curved solenoid.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: That inner result makes B proportional to r inside the wire and proportional to 1/r outside. The two formulas meet at the surface.  ·  A toroid uses a circular path inside the doughnut. The enclosed current is N I if the path threads all N turns. The circumference 2π r then gives B = μ0 N I /(2π r).  ·  A path that threads no current, such as a circle outside a toroid, gives zero line integral. With the symmetry, B itself is zero there in the ideal case.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Inside a thick wire the enclosed current is not the total current.  ·  The toroid uses total turns N, and the solenoid card used n per metre.  ·  A path with zero enclosed current is not automatically a zero field unless symmetry helps.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: r inside the wire is not the same formula as r outside.  ·  State inside or outside before choosing I_enc.  ·  Use N for the toroid and n for the solenoid.
